thesis: Every card that moves is billed twice: a wheel empties the hand and refills it, Brallin taxes the half that leaves and Shabraz taxes the half that arrives, and thirteen more permanents stand at the same two tollbooths.

stages.label: THIRTY-NINE SOURCES, TWO PRICES
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-six lands plus Sol Ring, Arcane Signet and Treasure Map // Treasure Cove. It pays for a 4- or 5-mana commander and then a 3-to-6-mana wheel on top, which is why mean available mana matters more here than any single land: 4.015 at turn four, 5.482 at turn six, 9.237 at turn ten, with the land drop hit at 0.810 on turn four and 0.698 on turn six. The map splits the landbase and the split is real, not an artefact: every land that charges LIFE to tap (City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Spire of Industry, Adarkar Wastes, Battlefield Forge, Shivan Reef), every any-colour source, and every land with a non-mana ability (Reliquary Tower, Talon Gates of Madara, Raugrin Triome, Opal Palace, Gemstone Caverns, Calciform Pools) is in THE FIXERS; not one of the twenty-two in COLOUR ON CURVE does any of those things. Two of the fixers are doing engine work a land has no business doing — Reliquary Tower is one third of the declared hand-size relief, and Raugrin Triome's cycling is a discard that pays Brallin. Both stay here because a land you must play on curve is mana first.

evidence.note: COLOUR ON CURVE, 22 lands, none charging life to tap
THE FIXERS, 14 lands: every life-tap, every any-colour source, every non-mana ability
Sol Ring, Arcane Signet and Treasure Map cluster in FUND THE NEXT WHEEL with the Treasure makers

stages.label: A WHEEL RESOLVING
stages.what_it_does: Seventeen cards move a whole hand at once; nothing else in the deck moves more than a few. That is the first thing that has to happen, because both commanders are guaranteed from the command zone and the wheel is the only variable — Brallin's mean cast turn is 4.255 and both partners are online by turn six 82.0% of the time, while a wheel is drawn by turn six 94.7% of the time at mean turn 1.735 and sits in 74.5% of opening sevens. So ignition is this deck's LEAST fragile stage, and any account that calls the wheel the bottleneck is wrong. Nine of the seventeen make you DISCARD, which is the half Brallin bills; the other eight shuffle or bottom the hand instead and pay him nothing (Arjun, Commit // Memory, Echo of Eons, Molten Psyche, Teferi's Puzzle Box, Time Reversal, Whirlpool Warrior, Winds of Change). The discard nine are drawn by turn six 82.1% of the time. A wheel with no tollbooth on the battlefield is just a new hand — the stage after this one is what makes it an engine.

evidence.note: all 17 sit in THE WHEELS; the city holds 6 more cards that do not wheel

stages.label: CARD MOVEMENT BETWEEN WHEELS, AND THE MANA FOR THE NEXT ONE
stages.what_it_does: A wheel is a burst; these keep cards moving on the turns there is no wheel, and pay for the one after. Three kinds. Outlets that convert mana into a discard one card at a time — Faithless Looting, Artist's Talent, Jaxis, Mindless Automaton, and Ceremonial Knife, whose Blood token is a discard and a draw in the same activation. Draw supply that keeps the tollbooths paid — Rhystic Study, Mind's Eye, Enduring Curiosity, Sorcerer Class, and Teferi's Ageless Insight, which doubles every card a wheel produces and was measured at +2.95 extra cards and +3.80 commander counters by turn ten. And Treasure that funds a second spell the same turn: Smothering Tithe, Generous Plunderer, Sticky Fingers. Library of Leng is here because it is what stops the cleanup step taking the wheel's seven back. Measured output of this stage plus ignition: 20.061 extra cards drawn and 10.444 cards discarded by turn ten. Caveat on the Treasure: `model_treasures` is OFF in goldfish_targets.json, so none of that mana is priced in any figure above.

evidence.note: 4 of 14 in FUND THE NEXT WHEEL
4 of 14 in WHAT THE DRAWS BUY
Artist's Talent, Faithless Looting and Teferi's Ageless Insight cluster with THE WHEELS on their draw/discard wording without being wheels

stages.label: THE TOLLBOOTHS THAT PAY IN BOARD AND CARDS
stages.what_it_does: Eleven permanents that read 'whenever you draw' or 'whenever you discard' and answer in counters, bodies or more cards. Shabraz is the per-draw half of the commander pair — a counter and a life per card arriving. Ivora is a second Brallin on the discard half (a counter per discard) and she makes her own fodder: the decomposition run priced her Blood alone at -0.026, her counter trigger alone at +0.305, and the two together at +0.817, which is the token feeding the trigger. Rielle converts a seven-card wheel discard into seven fresh draws, which then pay every per-draw trigger again. The Locust God, Improbable Alliance and Drake Haven turn card movement into fliers; Chasm Skulker and Ominous Seas bank it as counters; Containment Construct and Currency Converter recover the discarded card itself. This stage is where the deck's board comes from: mean bodies 2.280 at turn six and 7.202 at turn ten, mean board power 18.334 at turn ten, mean commander counters 32.765 at turn ten.

evidence.note: 3 of 11 in WHAT THE DRAWS BUY
Shabraz, Ivora and Chasm Skulker in BODIES THAT GROW; Brallin is in the same city but is in the output stage

stages.label: THE TOLLBOOTHS THAT PAY IN DAMAGE
stages.what_it_does: The same tollbooths, billing in life totals instead of board. Brallin is the whole discard half: one damage to EACH opponent per card discarded, so a seven-card wheel is seven to each of three seats. Glint-Horn Buccaneer is the only other per-discard damage source in the 99 and doubles that ping; Psychosis Crawler, Niv-Mizzet and Irencrag Pyromancer bill the draw half instead. Astral Drift is the one non-damage member — repeatable exile removal triggered by cycling — and it is here because what it produces is a targeted action, not fuel. Read the figures with their convention: the goldfish counts ONE opponent at 40 life, so cumulative discard-event damage of 13.22 by turn ten is a floor that roughly triples at a real table, and mean total damage of 31.290 at turn eight / 53.904 at turn ten is mostly COMBAT, not pings. The fragility is priced: Glint-Horn is the deck's single point of failure, a one-card component at 39.5% assembled and 18.4% by turn six.

evidence.note: Glint-Horn and Irencrag Pyromancer cluster with THE WHEELS; Brallin is in BODIES THAT GROW; Niv-Mizzet and Psychosis Crawler in WHAT THE DRAWS BUY; Astral Drift in CARD BY CARD. Five cards doing one job, four addresses.

stages.label: KEEPING THE TOLLBOOTH ON THE TABLE
stages.what_it_does: Two equipment that make a commander untargetable the turn it lands (Lightning Greaves' shroud, Swiftfoot Boots' hexproof), two counters that come stapled to a cycling cost so they are never a dead card (Decree of Silence, Nimble Obstructionist), and Nezahal, which cannot be countered, removes your maximum hand size, and whose self-exile cost is itself three discards — three more Brallin triggers paid to dodge a removal spell. The declared protection group is thin and measured thin: two cards, 61.9% assembled, 35.4% by turn six, mean turn 5.333. Held-up interaction is worse and the model says so — interaction castable sits at 0.083 on turn six and 0.125 on turn eight while 0.525 of hands HOLD an answer, because this model spends every mana it has. Read that as a floor, not a verdict.

evidence.note: 4 of 5 in CARD BY CARD; Nezahal clusters with THE WHEELS on its hand-size and draw wording

stages.label: THE AIR KILL, AND WHO CARRIES THE COUNTERS
stages.what_it_does: The declaration names two kills and they share one ignition. The WHEEL KILL is the output stage stacking pings; this stage is the AIR KILL — evasive bodies that grow on every card and fly over. Shark Typhoon, Vanguard Suppressor and Kefnet the Mindful fly; Silent Hallcreeper cannot be blocked; Stromkirk Noble, Marketback Walker, Waterbender Ascension and Gossip's Talent are the connect-and-grow support that makes the rest get through. The two commanders are the real finishers and they enable each other in a way no cluster shows: Shabraz's {W/U} gives a HUMAN flying and Brallin is a Human Shaman; Brallin's {R} gives a SHARK trample and Shabraz is a Shark Bird. Two 3/3s carrying 32.765 counters between them by turn ten, each granting the other the keyword it lacks. Measured clock, unopposed and against one seat: kill by turn seven 61.9%, by turn eight 87.3%, median turn 7, mean 7.268.

evidence.note: 5 of 8 in BODIES THAT GROW; Shark Typhoon and Vanguard Suppressor in WHAT THE DRAWS BUY, Kefnet in CARD BY CARD

lines.note: CLAIM, no passing stack. Seven cards discarded is seven separate Brallin triggers: seven damage to EACH opponent and Brallin at 10/10. The goldfish prices this against one 40-life seat and reads 13.22 cumulative discard-event damage by turn ten.
CLAIM, no passing stack. Both read 'whenever you discard a card', so the same seven discards bill twice. Glint-Horn is the deck's single point of failure: 39.5% assembled, 18.4% by turn six.

CLAIM, no passing stack. The doubler applies to every draw except the first in a draw step, so a wheel's seven becomes fourteen and Shabraz takes fourteen counters. Measured at +2.95 extra cards and +3.80 commander counters by turn ten.
CLAIM, no passing stack. Rielle's 'first discard each turn' fires once on the whole seven and draws seven, which then pays every per-draw tollbooth a second time on the same wheel.

CLAIM, no passing stack. Cracking a Blood token discards a card and draws one: a Brallin ping plus counter, an Ivora counter and a Shabraz counter from one activation. The decomposition run priced Blood alone at -0.026 and Blood plus trigger at +0.817.

CLAIM, no passing stack. Artist's Talent level 3 adds 2 to noncombat damage a source you control deals an opponent; Brallin's per-discard ping is noncombat damage to each opponent, so a seven-card wheel would read 21 a seat instead of 7. Unpriced — Artist's Talent is invisible to the goldfish.

CLAIM, no passing stack, and the one most worth checking. Library of Leng changes where a discarded card goes, not whether it was discarded; if that is right, a wheel pays Brallin its full count and you keep the cards on top of your library.
CLAIM, no passing stack. A symmetrical wheel makes three opponents draw seven each; every one of those 21 draws is a Treasure unless that player pays 2. Entirely unpriced: model_treasures is OFF.

CLAIM, no passing stack. The conversion half makes the damage half evasive and the damage half makes the conversion half trample: Shabraz's {W/U} targets a Human and Brallin is a Human Shaman; Brallin's {R} targets a Shark and Shabraz is a Shark Bird. 32.765 commander counters by turn ten sit on two 3/3s that can each give the other the keyword it lacks.

CLAIM, no passing stack. The air kill's bodies are made by the draw half, not cast: every card drawn is a 1/1 flying haste Insect off The Locust God, and Shark Typhoon cycles for an X/X flier at instant speed. Declared AIR KILL: 82.1% assembled, 53.5% by turn six, mean turn 4.871.

map_disagreements.component: THE WHEELS (city-2) is not the ignition stage
map_disagreements.why: All 17 wheels are in city-2, but city-2 holds 23 cards. The six extras cluster there on WORDING, not job: Teferi's Ageless Insight, Artist's Talent and Faithless Looting all say draw-and-discard without moving a hand, and Glint-Horn Buccaneer, Irencrag Pyromancer and Nezahal say it while being tollbooths or protection. Reading the city as the engine's first stage over-counts ignition by six.

map_disagreements.component: The damage tollbooths have four addresses
map_disagreements.why: Brallin, Glint-Horn, Irencrag, Niv-Mizzet, Psychosis Crawler and Astral Drift do one job — convert a card moving into a life total going down — and land in four cities, because the map reads what each card's trigger CONDITION is (a discard, a second draw, a cycle) rather than what it pays out. This is the deck's clock and it is invisible as a group on the map.

map_disagreements.component: The partners are split across two stages and one city
map_disagreements.why: Shabraz and Brallin sit together in city-3, correctly — both are commanders that grow on card movement. Functionally they are two different machines: Shabraz taxes the arriving half and pays in counters and life (conversion), Brallin taxes the leaving half and pays in damage (output). The city cannot show that, and it is the single most important thing to know about piloting the deck.

map_disagreements.component: Six cards discard themselves and the map scatters them
map_disagreements.why: Astral Drift, Decree of Silence, Nimble Obstructionist and Shark Typhoon in CARD BY CARD, Curator of Mysteries in WHAT THE DRAWS BUY, Raugrin Triome in THE FIXERS: every one is a card that cycles itself, which is a discard that pays Brallin and a draw that pays Shabraz at instant speed with no wheel. They are clustered on what they do WHEN cycled, which is six different things. The goldfish does not model cycling at all, so this whole channel is absent from every figure here.

map_disagreements.component: COLOUR ON CURVE and THE FIXERS are one mana stage but a real split
map_disagreements.why: Both cities are the landbase, so the mana stage cuts across them — but they are NOT an arbitrary division, and any account saying so is wrong on membership. Every land in the deck that charges life to tap, every any-colour source, and every land with a non-mana ability is in THE FIXERS; zero of the twenty-two in COLOUR ON CURVE does any of those. The split is cost-to-tap, which is a distinction a pilot uses every turn and a stage boundary cannot express.

open_questions.question: Does Library of Leng's replacement — putting a discarded card on top of your library instead of into the graveyard — still trigger Brallin's 'whenever you discard a card'? If it does, a wheel under Library of Leng pays its full damage AND leaves the cards on top.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the difference between Library of Leng being hand-size insurance and being the best card in the deck. Every damage figure for the wheel kill changes if this is wrong.

open_questions.question: Resolve a stack for the base line: a seven-card discard wheel with Brallin on the battlefield. Confirm that each card discarded is a separate trigger, that the damage is dealt to each opponent per trigger, and that the counters are on Brallin before the refill draws resolve.
open_questions.why_it_matters: This deck has ZERO passing stacks and zero verified pairings. Every line in this artifact is a claim; this is the one that must be a fact first, because six of the other eight depend on it.

open_questions.question: Does Artist's Talent level 3 ('if a source you control would deal noncombat damage to an opponent, it deals that much damage plus 2') apply per Brallin trigger, making a seven-card wheel 21 damage a seat rather than 7?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If it does, Artist's Talent is the deck's largest damage multiplier and it is currently INVISIBLE to the goldfish, so no figure in this artifact reflects it.

open_questions.question: Confirm the partner keyword grants: Shabraz's '{W/U}: Target Human gains flying' legally targets Brallin (Human Shaman) and Brallin's '{R}: Target Shark gains trample' legally targets Shabraz (Shark Bird).
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the whole air kill. Two 3/3s with 32.765 counters between them by turn ten only close a game if they are evasive, and the deck's answer is that each partner fixes the other.

open_questions.question: model-coverage reports Teferi's Ageless Insight as `invisible` (no channel reads it), while the card was measured at +2.95 extra cards and +3.80 commander counters by turn ten. Which is right — is there a doubler channel that model-coverage's channel table does not enumerate, or is the measured figure from a different run?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A card bought on a measured figure the coverage tool says was never read is the exact failure class the model_coverage gate exists to catch. If the figure stands, the tool is under-reporting; if it does not, one of the two cards added today is unpriced.

open_questions.question: Re-run with model_treasures and model_sacrifice ON. Five of the seven declared ramp cards make Treasure, Generous Plunderer is DARK on the treasure channel, Treasure Map // Treasure Cove is DARK on sacrifice, and Smothering Tithe off a symmetrical wheel is potentially the deck's largest single mana event.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every mana figure in the mana and fuel stages is a floor by an unknown amount, and the deck's ability to cast a second wheel the same turn rests entirely on the unpriced channel.

open_questions.question: How much is the deck losing by handing three opponents a fresh seven every wheel? The goldfish prices the tax and explicitly does not price the cost — it has no opponent turn and no opponent board.
open_questions.why_it_matters: A symmetrical wheel deck's real risk is the refill it gives a combo seat. Nothing in this artifact's figures can see it, and the answer decides whether the eight non-discard wheels are worth their slots at all.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: A DISCARD wheel drawn — the half that pays Brallin (six more shuffle or bottom and pay him nothing)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Change 'six more' to 'eight more' in the label.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Enumerated from the declaration's own two components: 17 wheels minus the 9 discard wheels is 8 — Arjun, Commit // Memory, Echo of Eons, Molten Psyche, Teferi's Puzzle Box, Time Reversal, Whirlpool Warrior, Winds of Change. The parenthetical undercounts the dead-for-Brallin half by two.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: THE AIR KILL — a wheel plus a flying body that grows on every card (second component)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Either drop Chasm Skulker from the component or reword it to 'an evasive body'.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Chasm Skulker has no flying and no evasion; its death tokens have islandwalk, not flying. The other three members — Shark Typhoon, The Locust God, Vanguard Suppressor — all do fly. A four-card component reading 81.9% by turn six is really three that match the label.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: A discard converted to board or cards (the non-damage half of the tax)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Split into two groups: TRIGGERS that fire on any discard (Containment Construct, Currency Converter, Drake Haven, Rielle) and OUTLETS you pay for one card at a time (Ceremonial Knife, Jaxis, Mindless Automaton).
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Only the triggers scale with a wheel — Rielle off a seven-card discard draws seven; Mindless Automaton off the same wheel does nothing, because its discard is an activation cost you pay separately. One 7-card group at 95.2% hides that the wheel-scaling half is 4 cards.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: the target list as a whole
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add a group for a per-discard TOLLBOOTH on the battlefield, naming Brallin, Ivora and Glint-Horn Buccaneer.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Eighteen nonlands are in no component at all, including BOTH COMMANDERS and both cards added today (Ivora, Insatiable Heir and Teferi's Ageless Insight). Ivora is a second Brallin on the discard half and nothing measures her; Teferi's Ageless Insight doubles every draw and nothing measures it.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: A real answer drawn — a counter, a sweeper or a tax
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: It is repeatable exile removal triggered by every cycle in the deck, and deck-audit already flags a protection-class card the taxonomy missed (Talon Gates of Madara). A 3-card answer group at 74.6% assembled is measuring less interaction than the deck holds.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Set model_treasures: true and model_sacrifice: true.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: The declaration's own ramp label says 'five of the seven of them Treasure the model is not reading', and model-coverage confirms it: Generous Plunderer DARK on treasure, Treasure Map // Treasure Cove DARK on sacrifice. A DARK count is the figure that invalidates a run.

notes: NO FACT TIER. engine-facts reports 0 verified pairings across 0 passing stacks, 0 load-bearing cards and 0 candidate combo lines. Every entry in `lines` is the analyst's reading, carries verified_by: null, and has a matching entry in open_questions.
Stage completeness: 100 of 100 cards placed, none unassigned. Counts: mana 39, ignition 17, fuel 14, conversion 11, output 6, protection 5, wincon 8.

NO FODDER STAGE. The resource this deck converts is its own hand, which is not a card class — there is no subset of the 99 whose job is to be eaten. The nearest thing, six cards that cycle themselves, are outlets and are filed under fuel, protection and output by what they do when cycled. Manufacturing a fodder stage here would name a city, not an engine.

The goldfish counts ONE opponent at 40 life, so every per-opponent figure (Brallin, Glint-Horn, Psychosis Crawler) is a floor that roughly triples at a four-player table. It also does not model cycling, madness, or activated loots — the whole self-discard channel is absent, not zero.

Two cards were cut from the 99 on 2026-09-14 (Elesh Norn // The Argent Etchings, Goblin Engineer) and neither appears anywhere in this artifact. The damage figures used here are the post-cut ones: damage@8 31.290, damage@10 53.904.

Figures are stated inside each stage's what_it_does rather than as evidence entries, because validate-engine's EVIDENCE_KINDS is the closed set {stack, combo, role, city} and has no figure kind. Sources: goldfish_metrics.json (10,000 iterations, seed 42, model_version a5dc923f4c9b, decklist_sha256 e512fc87f4) and deck-audit's engine block.
